items.body_md:
On August 12, one of the parties filed an Opposition or Response (Dkt. 71) to the Administrative Motion filed August 11 (Dkt. 70), completing a second paired administrative-motion cycle in less than a week and mirroring the Dkt. 68 / Dkt. 69 pairing covered yesterday. Neither filing's document text is publicly available through RECAP as of this writing, so the precise relief sought in Dkt. 70 — and the ground on which it is being opposed in Dkt. 71 — remains unverified beyond its procedural classification under Civil Local Rule 7-11. That classification governs the analysis: L.R. 7-11 is reserved for non-noticed administrative relief from case-management rules, not for contested merits disputes, and nothing in the docket captions signals a substantive claim, right, or obligation at stake. What is now clear is that both Administrative Motion cycles (Dkts. 68-69 and Dkts. 70-71) have drawn opposition, which means Judge Thompson will need to rule on each — neither resolved by consent. If either ruling touches the scope or timing of discovery, it becomes substantive under any materiality reading and will warrant immediate coverage. Absent the underlying documents, the safer read is that these oppositions are disputes over the administrative relief itself — page limits, filing accommodations, or analogous housekeeping — rather than over any discovery position.

The pattern is worth noting structurally: two separate administrative motions filed six days apart (August 6 and August 11), each opposed within four to five days. That cadence, against a September 18 fact-discovery close that is now thirty-six days out, suggests at least one side is pressing for procedural adjustments the other is resisting — consistent with the pre-cutoff friction common in IP discovery. 
The close of fact discovery is September 18, 2026.
 
Expert-report obligations follow in sequence: Opening Reports due October 30, 2026; Rebuttal Reports due December 18, 2026; and Close of Expert Discovery February 12, 2027.
 Any slippage to the September 18 cutoff would compress or shift each of those downstream dates and, more directly, would affect Getty's ability to complete the production record it needs to support damages quantification before any summary-judgment phase. Discovery disputes have been referred to Magistrate Judge Sallie Kim; if either motion crosses from administrative housekeeping into a genuine discovery dispute, that referral path is already in place.

The next concrete milestone is September 18, 2026 — close of fact discovery. Before that date, Judge Thompson (or Magistrate Judge Kim, if any administrative motion is re-characterized as a discovery dispute) will need to rule on both pending administrative motions. Those rulings are the next docket events worth watching.

items.body_md:
On August 11, Stability AI (or Getty — the filing party is not identified in the docket caption) filed a second Administrative Motion under Civil Local Rule 7-11 (Dkt. 70), one day after Getty or Stability filed an Opposition or Response to the first such motion (Dkt. 69, August 10), which itself was directed at the Administrative Motion filed August 6 (Dkt. 68). All three entries are procedural in character: Civil L.R. 7-11 is the mechanism for non-noticed relief from case-management rules — page limits, scheduling adjustments, sealing requests, and similar ministerial matters — and none of the docket descriptions signals a substantive dispute touching legal rights, claims, or the September 18 fact-discovery deadline. The opposition at Dkt. 69 does establish that whatever Dkt. 68 sought, the opposing party contested it, which upgrades the pairing from purely routine to worth monitoring; if Judge Thompson or Magistrate Judge Kim rules on Dkt. 68 in a way that affects discovery scope or timing, that order will warrant coverage. The documents themselves are not publicly available through RECAP as of this writing, so the precise relief sought in Dkts. 68 and 70 remains unverified beyond their procedural classification.

The more consequential backdrop is the fact-discovery clock. The close of fact discovery is set for September 18, 2026 — five weeks out — and the administrative motion cluster arriving in August is a common signal that at least one party is pressing for some form of relief (page extensions, filing accommodations, or, less commonly, a sealing dispute) ahead of that deadline. 
Discovery disputes have been referred to Magistrate Judge Sallie Kim, per Judge Thompson's May 4, 2026 Order of Reference.
 Any motion that crosses from administrative housekeeping into a genuine discovery dispute — scope of production, privilege, or a request to extend the September 18 cutoff — would move to Magistrate Kim and become substantive-and-important. Nothing on the current docket reaches that threshold yet.

The next concrete milestone is September 18, 2026 — close of fact discovery. If either Dkt. 68 or Dkt. 70 is seeking relief that touches that deadline, an order from Judge Thompson or Magistrate Kim could accelerate or compress the remaining schedule in ways that affect Getty's ability to build its damages record ahead of any summary-judgment phase.
